name: Introduzione
summary:
Formal Languages and Compilers is a course about the fundamentals of the theory underlying programming languages, and how they are translated to machine-readable code. It focuses on describing formal languages with regular expressions and grammars, how to recognize (or parse) a string belonging to such a language, how the parsing results are translated to a different language, and how the meaning (semantics) of programming languages are extracted and analyzed.

The topics of this course have important practical applications, and are also foundational to theoretical computer science.

Related courses are Code Transformation and Optimization (which is about how real-world compilers operate), Principles of Programming Languages (which is about programming language designs and paradigms), and Formal Methods for Software Engineering (which is about formalizing a program's behavior to ensure strong properties about it).

Weekly schedule

Lecture are delivered every week (except vacations) with the following calendar:

  • Tuesday, 08:30 - 10:00, room 2.0.1
  • Thursday, 10:30 - 12:00, room 26.1.1

All lectures are also streamed on WebEx and recorded, to benefit students that have contingencies (travel issues, work, sickness, overlapping lectures of other courses...). But we recommend participating in person.
